Lap Cheong may not be everyone's favorite but these homemade ones are very nice either eaten as is or added to a stir fry or fried rice.

I've modified this recipe to be more to my liking with less sweetness. Just add more of the sugar to it if you want a sweeter version.

If possible try to air dry the sausages by hanging them until dry and solid.

Ingredients

  • 375 g pork butt or shoulder
  • 75 g pork back fat (ask your butcher, they are normally happy to give it to you for free)
  • 1 tbsp brown sugar (packed)
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1/2 tsp five-spice powder
  • 1 tbl soy sauce
  • 2 tsp Shaoxing wine
  • 1 1/2 tbsp whiskey
  • 1 tsp water
  • Hog casings

Instructions

  1. Cut the pork meat into 0.5 cm squares and the fat into half that size (0.25 cm).
  2. Mix all other ingredients into a bowl and add the meat and fat.
  3. Put straight into the sausage casings, no need to rest it first.
  4. Place the sausages on a wire rack and prick them a bit to help with drying (not too much or they'll leak in the oven)
  5. Make sure they don't touch each other. Store in the fridge 12-24 h.
  6. Pre-heat the oven to 90 degree C (200 F).
  7. Put the sausages in for 5 hours and at the end just turn it off and let them cool for 2 hours. Don't open the oven during the entire 7 h period.
